name: Faber (Artificer Archetype)
body:
A faber sacrificed the depths of their arcane power to leverage their magic into creating and using veils in unorthodox ways.

Diminished Spellcasting

A faber casts one fewer artificer spell of each level than normal. If this reduces the number to 0, they may only cast artificer spells of that level if their Intelligence score provides bonus spells of that level. This alters spells.

The following two abilities, aessentiashaping and essence pool, replaces scribe scroll, magical artisan, and bonus metamagic feat.

Aessentiashaping (Su)

At 1st level, a faber has begun learning the secrets of akasha, utilizing a number of daily veil slots. They start play with 1 veil slot and gain an additional daily veil slot each day at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th. These veil slots can be used to shape any veil they know, such as those they learn using the Shape Veil feat, or those they prepare from their spellbook (see below) as part of shaping their veils each day. They can prepare and shape veils from their own spellbook much like preparing a spell. Additionally, they can shape veils from borrowed formula books and spellbooks if they succeed on a Knowledge Arcana skill check DC equal to the DC required to identify the scribed veil (typically DC 15). A faber can only prepare and shape their daily veils when they prepare their artificer spells.

When preparing and shaping veils from their spellbook, a faber uses their class level as their veilweaving level and their Intelligence modifier as their veilweaving modifier. The saving throw DC, if any, for veils a faber has prepared and shaped from their spellbook is equal to 10 + the essence invested in the veil + their veilweaving modifier.

Fabers do not have a list of known veils they can freely shape from; they learn and scribe qualifying veils within a spellbook from which they prepare and shape during their daily preparations, much akin to an arcane spellcaster preparing spells from a spellbook. Qualifying veils are those from the Vizier veil list and those with the Enhanced descriptor from the Kheshig and Soulforge veil lists. They do not gain the ability to shape Ring slot veils.

A faber is also limited in shaping veils using the veils slots granted by this archetype to only those that affect creatures (including themselves) or objects. To shape any of their veils from their spellbook, the faber must touch an object held or worn by a creature that corresponds to the veil’s chakra slot to affect them or the affected object if the veil targets objects. If the veil has an effect with a range greater than touch, it is reduced to touch; if a veil affects multiple targets, all affected targets must be touched.

Additionally, a faber cannot shape veils in their veil slots granted by this archetype that have any of the following traits or abilities:

Veils shaped in obscure chakra slots, such as Blood, Interface, Storm, Ring, or Voice slots.
Veils that have the Brand, Corrupt, Dao, Fleshwarp, Mark, or Title descriptors.
If the veil produces an area of effect other than emanation from the target(s) of the veil’s effects.

Scribing a veil to a spellbook functions much like scribing a spell to a spellbook (including scribing costs), and each veil has an effective spell level based on its chakra slots. Veils that can be shaped in multiple chakra slots are considered different veils for the purposes of scribing to a faber’s spellbook; one for each of their different slots (though they must follow the normal restrictions for duplicate veils when shaping those veils as normal). When shaping a veil inscribed in their spellbook, they can only shape and bind it in the chakra slots they have inscribed for that veil in their spellbook. Unlike a normal arcane spellcaster, a faber can scribe a veil to their spellbook of an effective spell level higher than the maximum spell level of artificer spells they can cast. For the faber, the effective spell levels for each chakra slot are shown below.

Effective Spell Level – chakra slot: 1st–Hands; 2nd–Feet and Head; 3rd–Wrists; 4th–Shoulders and Headband; 5th–Neck; and 6th–Belt.

A faber can always choose to scribe only the base effects of a veil to their spellbook, making it both easier and more affordable to learn. Base veils have an effective spell level of 0, no matter what chakra slot it is shaped to, but a shaped base veil can never be bound to its chakra. If a base veil that can be shaped in multiple chakra slots is inscribed in their spellbook, the chakra slot it is able to be shaped in is chosen as part of scribing it as a base veil. To shape a base veil in multiple different slots, it must be inscribed once for each slot.

Scribed veils can be copied from the formula book or spellbook of another aessentiamancy-using spellcaster (such as an aessentialist, aessentiamist, or spellspike magus), much like copying spells. They can also be learned from another veilweaver who has that veil shaped and is willing to demonstrate the effects of that veil for the duration it takes to scribe it. A faber must be able to identify the effects of the veil to know how to scribe it (whether it be by identifying the demonstrated veil or the scribed veil within a borrowed spellbook). In most cases, veilweavers charge a fee for the time spent demonstrating their veil in such detail that it can be scribed; this fee is usually equal to half the cost to inscribe a spell of the veil’s equivalent spell level into a spellbook.

Whenever a faber gains the ability to learn a 1st-level or higher artificer spell of their choice, such as those they begin the game with or gain through leveling up, they can choose to scribe a qualifying veil (see above) to their spellbook in lieu of any of those spells; the qualifying veil they scribe in this way must be of an effective spell level (see above) they can cast.

Essence Pool

At 1st level, a faber gains a pool of essence points which they can invest in their veils and essence receptacles to increase their power. They gain 1 point of essence at each class level.

The following three abilities, bestower of veils, improved essence capacity, and constrained research breakthrough, alters research breakthrough.

Bestower of Veils

At 2nd level, whenever a faber shapes a veil with the Enhanced descriptor from their spellbook, they may choose to modify the veil with the addition of the Title descriptor, allowing them to shape it on their allies. This supersedes the normal restrictions on Title veils from aessentiashaping and the range for entitling a Title veil is reduced to Touch range.

Improved Essence Capacity

At 3rd level, a faber’s growing knowledge of akasha has strengthened their mastery of essence. At 3rd level, and again at 9th and 15th level, their essence capacity increases by 1.

Constrained Research Breakthrough

At 5th level, a faber gains their first bonus feat from research breakthrough instead of 2nd and gains an additional bonus feat at 10th, 15th, and 20th level instead of every even level after 2nd. Additionally, a faber adds akashic feats to the list of options they may select whenever they gain a bonus feat from research breakthrough.

Selectable Chakra Binds

At 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, and 19th, a faber gains a selectable chakra bind. When they prepare and shape their veils from their spellbook for the day, a faber may choose one chakra bind slot for each selectable chakra bind they possess and they gain the ability to bind shaped veils from their spellbook to the chosen slots. They cannot select the same bind multiple times. The slots they may choose from are limited based on their class level, and the class level requirements to select each chakra bind slot are shown below.

Required Class Level – chakra bind slot: 2nd–Hands; 4th–Feet; 6th–Head; 8th–Wrists; 10th–Shoulders; 12th–Headband; 14th–Neck; and 16th–Belt.

Ring Mastery

At 5th level, a faber gains the ability to shape Ring veils using the veil slots granted by this archetype and can scribe those veils in their spellbook. Qualifying Ring veils must otherwise still abide by the constraints for what counts as a qualifying veil as described in the faber’s aessentiashaping ability. At 11th level, a faber may choose Ring as a chakra bind slot for one of their selectable chakra binds. This ability replaces retain charge.
